# How Connected Request and Credential Management Helps Teams


November 04, 2026


by Julie Crump


##


Automating the follow-up on incoming requests and expiring credentials helps teams ensure nothing slips through the cracks.


## The Requests and Credentials a Small Team Tracks by Hand


In a small local government, the same person who logs a resident’s pothole complaint in the morning may spend the afternoon confirming a contractor’s insurance is current before a permit is approved. Two very different responsibilities, fielding incoming requests from residents and verifying the credentials of contractors and professisonals, often land on the same desk.


Both depend on consistent follow-up, and follow-up is often the first thing to suffer when a team is stretched thin. On a normal week, the same person is also:


- Routing incoming resident requests to the correct department
- Following up on requests and approvals that have sat longer than they should
- Confirming contractor and professional credentials are current before work is approved
- Tracking dozens of license expiration dates so a lapse does not hold up a project


When routing and verification are manual, the items that slip are the ones no one was actively monitoring: a request passed from one department to another, or a credential that quietly expired.


## With the Code Enforcement and Request Manager modules, our team has unlocked features that will increase productivity, foster community connection, and encourage collaboration between our government agency and our residents.


Crandall, Texas


## What Changes When Requests Route and Escalate Automatically


When resident and staff requests run through one connected system, every request enters through a single point and routes to the right department automatically. Requests escalate on their own if they pass a deadline, so nothing depends on someone remembering to check. Residents submit and track their own requests through a public portal so fewer status calls reach the counter, and more requests route without manual work. Automation enables a lean team to keep up with a volume of requests that manual handoffs could never sustain.


## How Projects Stay on Track When the System Flags Credential Lapses


Credentials work the same way, but in reverse. Rather than requests coming in from residents, credentials must be confirmed before work goes out. When credential management runs inside the platform, contractor and professional credentials are validated before work is approved. The system tracks every expiration, sending reminders before a lapse. Because the check happens within the workflow, an expired or missing credential is flagged before work is approved rather than being discovered after it starts. The verification that once depended on someone to remember becomes a step the system manages automatically.


## Where Requests and Credentials Slow a Team Down


Connecting request and credential follow-ups does not require replacing everything at once. Streamlining processes starts with finding where requests stall and where a credential expiration could slip past unnoticed. A few questions tend to surface the biggest gaps:


- When a request belongs to more than one department, how is it routed today?
- How quickly can staff tell a resident where their request stands?
- Before work is approved, how is a contractor’s or professional’s credential status confirmed?
- If a credential expires mid-project, how does the team ensure work stops?
